name: SDLC
description: Story-first engineering with the evidence behind each step, in twelve skills. story writes each change as As a / I want / so that, its context, numbered rules each with Given/When/Then examples in concrete values, and an Out of scope list, asking wherever a result is not in the request, the code or a tool, splits or reviews stories, then builds each one: the session fixes the interface, it writes failing tests through it from the acceptance criteria by failing-tests and locks them, a fresh agent adds tests for wrong implementations they let pass, then the code, a refactor, a review by three fresh agents that a fourth checks, then a push and a pull request into main. bug reproduces a reported bug, decides fix now, story or won't fix, builds the fix through story, then finds why it escaped and proposes the criterion, check or ADR that closes the gap, and sorts a bug backlog the same way. refactoring names each smell with the lines that show it, refactors only what a change in hand or a hotspot justifies, in small named steps with the tests green after each, and commits structure apart from behaviour. using-trackers files each story or spike as one labelled issue on Gitea, GitHub, GitLab or Jira, orders the issues by the tracker's own blocking relation with no epic, and reads every write back. adr records each expensive decision with the user's reasons. spike answers one question with throwaway code inside a timebox and keeps only the findings. orient writes AGENTS.md with only what an agent cannot learn by reading the repository, and a one-page architecture snapshot in ARCHITECTURE.md, traced from the code, its outside callers and the systems it calls. guardrails turns each rule into a check, a path-scoped rule or an AGENTS.md line, blocks any commit holding a secret with a gitleaks pre-commit hook, and runs the checks when Claude ends its turn and before it opens a pull request. review-code reviews stories, pull requests, the user's own code and designs the same way: three fresh agents check each stated acceptance criterion blind to each other, one searching hardest for security, and a fourth keeps only the findings a red test or a cited line proves. new-project starts a new repository from the user's template for its language, Python today, renames the template's placeholders and pushes the first commit once the checks pass. handing-off writes a handoff document when context fills or work stops partway, recording the dead ends a fresh session would otherwise rediscover. A hook lists each ADR still in force at the start of every session.
